title: Three Ways to Iterate
goal: iter borrows, iter_mut borrows mutably, into_iter takes ownership.

sections.text: Every collection offers three iterator families, and they differ in ownership. `.iter()` borrows: items arrive as `&T`, and the collection stays usable afterwards. `.iter_mut()` borrows mutably: items arrive as `&mut T`, for editing in place. `.into_iter()` takes ownership: items arrive as `T`, and the collection is consumed.

sections.caption: Borrowing iteration leaves the collection alive.

sections.text: A `for` loop uses `into_iter()` behind the scenes. Writing `for w in words` moves the whole `Vec`, so using `words` after the loop is a use of a moved value, `E0382`. Writing `for w in &words` iterates borrowed items and the collection survives.

The decision is the same ownership decision as always: if you need the collection afterwards, borrow it with `.iter()` or `&`. If the loop is the collection's last user, let `into_iter()` consume it. Cloning the collection first is the expensive way to avoid making this decision.

explanation: iter borrows, iter_mut edits in place, into_iter consumes. A bare for loop consumes; iterate over a reference to keep the collection.
